newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: FORECAST - Yugo 1996 inflation seen at 95 percent.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Yugo 1996 inflation seen at 95 percent.

text.p: A Belgrade Economic Institute on Monday revised its 1996 inflation forecast upwards from 85 to 95 percent compared with the government's estimate of 60 percent.
Zoran Popov, a member of the institute told Reuters the forecast was based on a projected three to 3.5 percent rise in retail prices in November and two percent in December.
According to federal statistics, retail prices in October rose 1.4 percent against 1.2 percent in September with an October year-on-year rise of 69.6 percent.
Inflation for the first 10 months of 1996 rose 102.3 percent against the same period last year.
Popov said monthly inflation had slowed and the year-on-year inflation rate was declining.
"The rise of retail prices in October can be defined here as a low inflation," he said, but added that there were fears inflation would not remain at such low level.
The electricity consumption quota to be applied in November will increase the price of electricity by 47 percent, he said.

According to Popov, this will push retail prices up two percent. "As we expect prices of other goods to rise between one and two percent, we forecast November inflation not to be under three percent."
The government last month forecast 60 percent annual inflation, or half the 1995 figure. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom ++381 11 222 4254
